churches.assessment: All Saints Church in New Holland, PA (Lancaster County) was established in 1999 as a church plant of Christ Church (Moscow, ID) and is a member of the CREC. Dr. Gregg Strawbridge served faithfully as pastor for twenty years (2002–2022) and is the founder of the Strawbridge Ministerial Forum hosted by the church. Following his passing in 2022, Rev. Kasey Horvath (lead) and Rev. Brandon Gilanyi (associate) were installed in 2023, and the congregation relocated to a historic building in New Holland in 2024. Theologically this is a classic Moscow-network CREC congregation: Reformed, covenant-renewal liturgical worship, paedocommunion, classical Christian education ethos, patriarchal household vision, and postmillennial cultural engagement. The one area calling for direct inquiry is soteriology — CREC churches have historically been associated with Federal Vision theology, which modifies traditional Reformed articulations of justification. Ask the elders directly about their position on FV and justification. For a Reformed man in Lancaster County seeking a serious, liturgical, Moscow-aligned CREC home, this is the obvious first visit.
churches.gender_detail: Patriarchal household vision, male headship, anti-feminist. Male-only pastors/elders (Horvath, Gilanyi).

churches.assessment: Bethany Grace Fellowship in East Earl, Pennsylvania is one of the founding congregations of the Alliance of Mennonite Evangelical Congregations (AMEC) — the conservative Anabaptist-evangelical body that broke from the Mennonite Church USA merger in 2002 over doctrinal and sexuality concerns. Founded in 1957 as Blue Ball Mennonite Church, renamed Bethany Mennonite, and now Bethany Grace Fellowship, the congregation is led by Lead Pastor Steve Benedict. AMEC's two-fold confessional commitment — to evangelical orthodoxy and to historic biblical Anabaptism — gives this church the theological clarity that newer MC USA progressive drift lacks. For a Lancaster County man wanting a complementarian, biblically-grounded, Anabaptist-pietist congregation with explicit orthodoxy commitments and full ministry portfolio, Bethany Grace Fellowship is a strong candidate.

churches.assessment: Butter Valley Community Church in Bally, Pennsylvania — formerly known as Hereford Mennonite Church — was the leading congregation that organized the Alliance of Mennonite Evangelical Congregations (AMEC) in 2001-2002 when conservative Anabaptists departed Mennonite Church USA over doctrinal and sexuality concerns. Robert Gerhart, then-pastor, was the primary AMEC organizer. Today Pastor Mark Hager leads with Caleb McCarthy as Associate Pastor. AMEC's two-fold confessional commitment to evangelical orthodoxy and historic biblical Anabaptism gives this congregation rare theological clarity for a Mennonite-rooted body. For a Berks County or Boyertown-area man wanting a complementarian, biblically-grounded, Anabaptist-pietist congregation with explicit orthodoxy heritage, Butter Valley is one of the strongest options in southeastern Pennsylvania.

churches.name: Cornerstone Presbyterian Church (OPC)
churches.denomination_detail: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — Presbytery of Philadelphia

score_notes.christology: OPC subscribes to the Westminster Standards — orthodox Trinitarian Christology, Chalcedonian two-natures, virgin birth, bodily resurrection.
score_notes.scripture: Westminster Confession ch. 1 affirms plenary verbal inspiration and inerrancy of the Scriptures as the only rule of faith and life.
score_notes.gender: OPC Book of Church Order restricts the offices of teaching elder, ruling elder, and deacon to qualified men only (1 Tim 2–3; Titus 1).
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of ordained male elders (session) under presbyterian polity with accountability to the presbytery and General Assembly.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed soteriology per Westminster — monergistic regeneration, sola fide, sola gratia, sola Scriptura, effectual calling, perseverance of the saints.
score_notes.cultural: OPC historically resists theological accommodation to cultural pressure — Machen's legacy of confessional fidelity over cultural relevance.
score_notes.denominational: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — founded 1936 by J. Gresham Machen as a confessionally Reformed denomination against Modernism in the PCUSA.
score_notes.preaching: OPC pulpits are characterized by expository, Christ-centered, Law/Gospel preaching from the Westminster tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: OPC congregations typically emphasize family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church — strong formation pipeline for men.
score_notes.mission: OPC Committee on Foreign Missions and Home Missions actively plants confessionally Reformed churches domestically and abroad.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Presbyterian Church (OPC) is a congregation of the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), the confessional Reformed denomination founded in 1936 by J. Gresham Machen. OPC churches subscribe to the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms, restrict ordained office to qualified men, and practice presbyterian polity with accountability through session, presbytery, and General Assembly. Baseline green rating reflects confessional identity; verify local particulars on the website.
churches.enrichment_notes: Added from OPC.org locator and Presbytery of Philadelphia directory; baseline green rating per OPC confessional identity.

churches.name: Faith Bible Fellowship Church of York
churches.pastor_credentials: BA Elizabethtown College, MS South University, MA Liberty University, EdD Eastern University

score_notes.christology: Trinitarian orthodoxy. Affirms Apostles' Creed. Christ alone for salvation.
score_notes.scripture: Bible as final authority. Adheres to BFC 28 Articles of Faith. High view of Scripture.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Elder Alex Kocman leads men's discipleship groups at the church. Confirmed by personal relationship with user — Kocman, who writes publicly at American Reformer and Founders Ministries on biblical manhood, carries that conviction into hands-on men's formation inside the local body.
score_notes.soteriology: Doctrines of grace (TULIP). Salvation by grace through faith alone. Reformed soteriology.
score_notes.gender: Patriarchal household vision, male headship, anti-feminist. Church mission statement is explicitly household-focused: 'joyfully build Christ's kingdom, household by household.' Male-only elders and pastors per BFC bylaws. Elder Alex Kocman is a published voice at American Reformer and Founders Ministries on biblical manhood, male headship, and the missions-critical nature of complementarian/patriarchal order. The church holds a complementarian label but with appropriate biblical-patriarchy guardrails — the hard line on male-only elder rule, an unapologetic household-by-household mission, and Kocman's public writing against the cultural crisis of masculinity — that prevent the usual drift of soft complementarianism into functional egalitarianism. Caveat: church retains a female servant-deacon (Helen Gemmill); by BFC polity deacons 'do not exercise rule or spiritual authority,' so this is a serving role rather than an office of authority.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led with 3 elders (Senior Pastor + 2). Deacon board for material needs. Denominational accountability through BFC.
score_notes.preaching: Expository, sermon-based teaching through Scripture. Reformed tradition. Podcast sermons available.
score_notes.mission: Church planting emphasis. Elder Alex Kocman directs communications for ABWE (international missions). Bold witness central.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT language. Conservative Reformed stance. Family-focused mission statement.
score_notes.denominational: Bible Fellowship Church denomination. Accountable to BFC conference. Self-governing under elder board.

churches.assessment: Faith Bible Fellowship Church of York is a Reformed, evangelical, baptistic church in the BFC denomination. Pastor Wesley Bunting leads a solid elder-governed congregation committed to the doctrines of grace and expository preaching. The church's mission — 'joyfully build Christ's kingdom, household by household' — reflects a patriarchal, family-centered, Great Commission focus. Elder Alex Kocman's role with ABWE, his published work at American Reformer and Founders Ministries, and his hands-on men's discipleship leadership give the church unusually strong DNA on biblical manhood, male headship, and international missions. The one polity detail worth asking about directly: the church retains a female servant-deacon (Helen Gemmill) under BFC's rule that deacons 'do not exercise rule or spiritual authority' — elder rule remains entirely male. Doctrinally and practically, green across the board. Worth visiting.
churches.gender_detail: Patriarchal household vision, male headship, anti-feminist. Male-only elders (Wesley Bunting, Alex Kocman, Joshua Vann). Female servant-deacon (Helen Gemmill) on board — non-authority role per BFC polity.

churches.assessment: Grantham Church is the historic flagship of the Brethren in Christ U.S. denomination, founded near the campus of what is now Messiah University in Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania. Pastor David Flowers brings a serious academic-pastoral pedigree — biblical studies graduate degrees, 25+ years across Texas, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, and a published trajectory in New Testament studies and early Christian ethics. The Brethren in Christ tradition holds together Anabaptist peace witness with Wesleyan-Holiness soteriology and pietist devotion — a hybrid that produces mission-minded, Bible-loving congregations but with synergistic rather than Reformed soteriology. For a Mechanicsburg-area man wanting a Christ-centered, mission-oriented church with a graduate-degreed expositor in the pulpit, Grantham deserves a careful look. The denominational yellow flag is gender — BIC USA does permit women's ordination at congregational discretion, though Grantham's senior pastoral office is male.

churches.assessment: Harrisburg Brethren in Christ Church is a city-center congregation under Pastor Hank Johnson, who came up through this very church — first as Youth Pastor (2008), then Pastor of Discipleship & Youth (2013), and finally Senior Pastor (November 2018). His backstory is striking: born in Monrovia, Liberia, he and his family lived as immigrants and refugees through Sierra Leone and Côte d'Ivoire before settling in Palisades Park, NJ and Philadelphia. His MDiv and his work on the BIC Historical Society board and as Atlantic Conference assistant moderator suggest a serious denominational pastor. For a Harrisburg-area man wanting a Bible-rooted, urban, mission-oriented church under male senior leadership in the Anabaptist-Holiness tradition, Harrisburg BIC merits a careful visit. Denominational yellow on gender remains because BIC USA permits women's ordination.

churches.assessment: Indian Valley Faith Fellowship in Harleysville, Pennsylvania has been led by Senior Pastor Dean Landry since July 2014, after his 16+ years of pastoral ministry at a church in Northern Michigan. Pastor Landry holds a B.A. from Baptist Bible College of PA and two graduate degrees — from Bethel College and Grand Rapids Theological Seminary. Family Pastor Nate Paine fills out the multi-pastor team. The Alliance of Mennonite Evangelical Congregations (AMEC) represents the conservative Anabaptist-evangelical body that broke from Mennonite Church USA in 2002 over doctrinal and sexuality concerns — its two-fold confessional commitment is to evangelical orthodoxy and historic biblical Anabaptism. For a Montgomery County or Harleysville-area man wanting a complementarian, biblically-grounded, Anabaptist-pietist church with a graduate-degreed expository pastor, Indian Valley Faith Fellowship is a strong candidate.
